newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House bill introduced to help fund Amtrak.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House bill introduced to help fund Amtrak.

text.p: A bipartisan bill to divert part of the federal gasoline tax to help fund Amtrak, the government-subsidized national rail passenger service, was introduced in the House Thursday.

The bill would raise $3.9 billion over five years by reallocating one-half cent per gallon of the federal gasoline tax. Amtrak would use the money to buy new rail equipment and make other capital improvements.
House sponsors included Rep. Michael Castle, a Delaware Republican, and Ben Cardin, a Maryland Democrat.

The same bill has been introduced in the Senate by William Roth, a Delaware Republican who is chairman of the Senate Finance committee, and Daniel Patrick Moynihan, a New York Democrat who is the panel's ranking minority member.
Amtrak Chairman Thomas Downs told a Finance Committee hearing Wednesday the additional money was essential to keep the rail service in business.
"Amtrak is in difficult shape," Downs said. "We cannot preserve a national passenger rail system through yet another year of inadequate funding."

Downs said Amtrak was already borrowing money to meet its payroll and needed several billion dollars in coming years to complete a modernization effort that includes buying 18 high speed trains for its busy East Coast corridor.
